rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Test the high-temperature endpoint against injection 1 to assess whether temperature separates the early cluster. Shorter retention should also provide time margin for a shallower gradient if needed.

Combine the favorable temperature selectivity with a shallower gradient to improve the remaining critical pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, allowing full resolution without a time penalty.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a higher starting organic fraction to change its selectivity. The first peak was retained sufficiently to justify this moderate increase in phi0.
Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Monitor the early critical pairs, which have only modest resolution margins.

Slightly narrow the gradient window to recover the small resolution deficits in injection 6 while retaining most of its speed advantage. The final organic fraction remains well above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.
Reduce phi1 one more step to bring the remaining critical pair above R = 1.5. This intermediate gradient slope should yield full resolution with an earlier last peak than injection 5.
